paper.title: Decision Making Problems with Funnel Structure: A Multi-Task Learning Approach with Application to Email Marketing Campaigns

unmapped: Each arm a has a funnel of J layers: z_j ~ Bernoulli(mu(x^T theta_{a,j})), observations r_j = prod_{s<=j} z_s; the reward is r_J (mean P_J = product of layer GLM means)
Learner observes all J cumulative layer signals of the pulled arm (multi-layer auxiliary feedback)
Joint layer parameters lie in a known hypothesis class Theta_0 (sequential or clustered dependency with radii q_j)
Link mu monotone with c_mu <= mu' <= kappa; contexts bounded by d_x
Minimum eigenvalue of the expected covariance lower bounded by lambda_bar
settings.definition_quote: Our contextual bandit with funnel structure is denoted by $M = \{\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{X}, P_x, \{F_a\}_{a \in \mathcal{A}}\}$, where $\mathcal{A}$ is the finite action space with $|\mathcal{A}| = A$, $\mathcal{X}$ is the common context space, $P_x$ is the context distribution and each arm $a \in \mathcal{A}$ is assigned a funnel ... On each round of $t$-th interaction, the environment generates a context $x_t \sim P_x$, the agent takes an action $a_t$ and the funnel $F_{a_t}$ returns the reward vector $(r_{1t}, \dots, r_{Jt})$

settings.name_in_paper: Supervised learning on a single funnel (prediction error)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Passive supervised learning (prediction error of a multi-task GLM estimator on a fixed dataset), not an interactive bandit problem.
unmapped: Multi-task GLM estimation across J funnel layers with imbalanced sample sizes n_j
Joint parameter in a known hypothesis class Theta_0 (sequential or clustered dependency)
settings.definition_quote: Before discussing the contextual bandits with funnel structure, we first consider the supervised learning scenario for a single funnel and seek a bound for the prediction error of each layer: $\text{PE}_j = |\mu(x^T \theta_j^*) - \mu(x^T \hat \theta_j)|$

conditions: Assumptions 1-4: GLM layers, mu monotone with c_mu <= mu' <= kappa, ||x|| <= d_x, true joint parameter in Theta_0
minimum eigenvalue of expected covariance lower bounded by lambda_bar

source.quote: Using Algorithm \ref{algo:mt_cb}, under the Assumptions 1-4, with a probability at least $1-\delta$, the total regret ... \leq 2\sqrt{2}c_{0} \sum_{a, j} \sqrt{n_{a, j}^{T}} + \sum_{a, j} \frac{8c_0^2Jd_x^4 \log (6AJT / \delta)}{ \bar p_{a, j}^2} - \sum_{a, j} \Delta_{a, j}.

results.notes: Full version of Theorem 3 in the appendix. Regret is measured through mean conversion probabilities P_J but holds with probability 1-delta. The paper is inconsistent about the constants: c_0 uses c_{delta/AJT} here but c_{delta/3AJT} in Theorem 3, and pbar is defined with P_{J-1} here vs P_{j-1} in Theorem 3. The bound depends on random pull counts and on the data-dependent benefit term.

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Using Algorithm \ref{algo:mt_cb}, under the Assumptions 1-4, with high probability, the total regret ... = \mathcal{O} (c_{0} \sum_{a, j} \sqrt{n_{a, j}^{T}} + \sum_{a, j} \frac{c_{0}^{2} J d_{x}^{4}}{\bar{p}_{a, j}^{2}}) - \sum_{a, j} \Delta_{a, j}

results.notes: The O hides constants and log factors. The subtracted benefit term lies outside the O in the paper. The paper says this reduces to sqrt(AT) when J=1.

source.label: lem:pred_err
source.quote: Using the model defined above, assume $J = 1$ and the true parameter $\theta^* \in \Theta_0$. ... Then with a probability at least $1-\delta$, we have $|\mu(x^T\hat \theta) - \mu(x^T\theta^*)| \leq \kappa \min \{ d_x q, \|x\|_{M_n^{-1}} \frac{c_{\delta}}{c_{\mu}}\sqrt{\frac{d}{n}}\}$ ... $c_{\delta} = 80d_x\sqrt{2\ln(8/\delta)}$.

results.notes: Bound on the prediction error at x. The first line of the lemma has a factor 4 in the parametric term that disappears in the second line. Recorded the final displayed bound.

symbols.lambda_min: lower bound on min eigenvalue of M_{j,n_j} (Assumption 5)
symbols.n_j: number of observations of layer j

conditions: sequential dependency with radii q_1 >= ... >= q_J

source.label: thm:seq_thm
source.quote: For any funnel with a sequential dependency of parameters $q_1, \dots, q_J$ ... If $n_{j+1} \leq n_j / 4$, $q_1 \geq, \dots, \geq q_J $ and Assumption 5 is satisfied, then with a probability at least $1-\delta$, for any $j_0 \in [J]$, we have $\text{PE}_j \leq \kappa \|x\|_2 \frac{ c_{\delta/J}}{c_{\mu}\lambda} \sqrt{\frac{d}{n_j}}, \text{ if } j < j_0$

results.notes: Prediction error of layer j. The appendix restatement (Theorem 4) uses c_delta instead of c_{delta/J}.

symbols.lambda_min: lower bound on min eigenvalue of M_{j,n_j}
symbols.n_j0: number of observations of threshold layer j_0

conditions: sequential dependency with radii q_1 >= ... >= q_J

source.label: thm:seq_thm
source.quote: \kappa\|x\|_2(\frac{ c_{\delta/J}}{c_{\mu}\lambda} \sqrt{\frac{d}{n_{j_0}}} + \sum_{i = j_0 + 1}^{j} q_i), \text{ if } j \geq j_0, where we let $n_0 = \infty$.

results.notes: The bound is tightest when j_0 is the smallest j satisfying the threshold condition (Eq. condition).

symbols.lambda_min: lower bound on min eigenvalue of M_{j,n_j}
symbols.n_j0: observations of layer j_0 = argmin_j c_delta/(c_mu lambda) sqrt(d/n_j) + q_j

source.label: thm:clst_thm
source.quote: For any funnel with a clustered dependency of parameters $q_1, \dots, q_J$, let $\hat \theta_1, \dots, \hat \theta_J$ be the estimates from Algorithm \ref{algo:mt_funnel}. With a probability at least $1-\delta$, $\text{PE}_j \leq \kappa\|x\|_{2}\min\{\frac{c_{\delta / J}}{c_{\mu} \lambda} \sqrt{\frac{d}{n_{j_{0}}}}+q_j, \frac{c_{\delta / J}}{c_{\mu} \lambda} \sqrt{\frac{d}{n_{j}}}\}$

results.notes: Uses lambda from Assumption 5 implicitly, although the theorem does not cite it.

source.label: cor:1
source.quote: Let $\hat \theta_1, \dots, \hat \theta_J$ be the estimates from Algorithm \ref{algo:mt_funnel} and $\Theta_1$ be the set defined in Algorithm \ref{algo:mt_funnel}. With a probability at least $1-\delta$, for all $j \in [J]$, we have \text{PE}_j \leq \kappa \min \{ \sup_{\theta_1, \theta_2 \in \Theta_1[j]} |x^T(\theta_1 - \theta_2)|, \|x\|_{M_n^{-1}} \frac{c_{\delta}}{c_{\mu}}\sqrt{\frac{d}{n_j}}\}.

results.notes: General prediction-error bound for the multi-task estimator.
